entrypoints.summary: A build-controlled workspace directory name reaches SSH-wrapper generation on a Unix agent when the Manually provided keys Git host-key verification strategy is selected.
The fixed strategy source identifies the Manually provided keys strategy as an administrator-supplied host-key verifier.

negative_controls: Generated wrapper omits the malicious workspace name.
Generated wrapper references the SSH-key environment variable.
Designated evidence file is absent after test wrapper execution.
observability.positive_marker: The related fixed-wrapper test uses a payload intended to create a designated evidence file if injected shell text executes.

preconditions: The attacker can influence the build working-directory name.
The affected workflow runs on a Unix Jenkins agent.
The Manually provided keys Git host-key verification strategy is in use.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A workspace path component containing shell command-substitution or other shell-control syntax.
trigger_steps.summary: Supply a workspace name containing shell metacharacters such as command substitution, then cause Git client SSH-wrapper generation.

capabilities.concept: shell syntax injection into generated SSH wrapper
OS command execution as Jenkins agent

impacts.concept: compromise of Jenkins agent execution context

relation_candidates.dst: shell syntax injection into generated SSH wrapper
relation_candidates.rationale: The advisory identifies incorrect escaping of the workspace directory name while embedding it in the SSH wrapper.

relation_candidates.dst: OS command execution as Jenkins agent
relation_candidates.rationale: The advisory describes command substitution leading to command execution on Jenkins agents.

relation_candidates.dst: compromise of Jenkins agent execution context
relation_candidates.rationale: Commands run under the affected agent process identity affect that execution context.

impact.affected_asset: Jenkins agent process and resources accessible under its process identity
impact.attacker_capability: Execute commands selected through a workspace-name shell payload, subject to control of the build working-directory name and use of the affected verification strategy
impact.security_effect: OS command execution on an affected Jenkins agent

causal_trace.summary: An attacker-controlled workspace directory name is used in the affected Git-client workflow.
The workspace-derived directory name is embedded in a generated SSH wrapper without correct shell escaping, so a filesystem-name value can become shell syntax.

The generated Unix SSH wrapper is interpreted by a shell; the fixed regression suite models command-substitution, command-chaining, and quote-escape workspace names and invokes the production Unix wrapper generator.
Shell command substitution from the workspace name can execute attacker-selected OS commands under the Jenkins agent process identity.

failure.operation: Shell parsing of workspace-derived text in a generated Unix SSH wrapper

primary_invariant.statement: A build-controlled workspace path must not be emitted as shell-program text such that shell parsing can interpret its characters as commands or substitutions.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The advisory states that the plugin did not correctly escape the workspace directory name when embedding it in a generated SSH wrapper.

quality.review_notes: The official advisory supports affected/fixed scope, the workspace-to-wrapper escaping mechanism, the Manually provided keys precondition, and agent command-execution impact. The rendered comparison artifact does not expose a patch hunk or vulnerable source line. The available executable regression test is annotated SECURITY-3614 rather than SECURITY-3723; it is retained only as closely related fixed-wrapper oracle evidence, not as proof that a SECURITY-3723 test ran or passed.

remediation.invariant_restored: The fixed regression suite requires wrapper text to reference the SSH-key environment variable rather than contain the malicious workspace name directly, and checks that execution does not create the payload evidence file.
mitigation_classes: avoid direct interpolation of workspace-derived paths into generated shell wrappers
use environment-variable references in wrapper scripts

target.component: Unix-agent SSH wrapper generation when using Manually provided keys host-key verification

oracle.channel: generated wrapper content and filesystem evidence-file check
oracle.expected_negative: The fixed suite expects the generated wrapper to reference the SSH-key environment variable, omit the malicious workspace name, and leave the designated evidence file absent after wrapper execution.
oracle.expected_positive: For a vulnerable implementation that emits the malicious workspace name into shell wrapper text, executing a command-substitution payload could create its designated evidence file.
